newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Simex Eurodollars, Euroyen end flat in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Simex Eurodollars, Euroyen end flat in thin trade.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures, already in overbought territory after Thursday's sharp run-up, ended steady after trading in a four-tick band all Friday.
The benchmark December contract ended unchanged against its CME close of 99.31. Volume was an estimated 11,384 contracts.
The release of weak industrial output data for August and September reinforced the market view that the Bank Of Japan is unlikely to hike interest rates soon, dealers said.
Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry said manufacturing output was seen down 1.2 percent month-on-month in August and September was seen up 0.1 percent month-on-month.
"The euroyen is overbought technically, particularly in the back months but it can still go higher because there is no sign of a sharp pull-back," said one dealer with a U.S. house.

Japanese government bond futures ended firmer after being bought back following the release of the industrial production figure. September ended at 122.56 against its open at 122.20. Eurodollars ended flat after a sell-off in Chicago overnight on renewed fears of a possible rate hike by the Federal Reserve before the end of the year.
The rate fears were triggered by a stronger than expected upward revision in second quarter gross domestic product growth to 4.8 percent from 4.2 percent previously.
"There wasn't much going on in the dollar pit," said one dealer with a U.S.house. "It was the case in the last few days with the market correcting after the movement in Chicago," he said.
December ended at 94.05, unchanged from its IMM close. Volume was 7,565 contracts. -- Valerie Lee (65 8703080)
